comment: The usual suspects: folders that grow quietly and mostly come back on their own. Paths are relative to the scan root (normally the user's home folder). Add your own rules to ~/Library/Application Support/Jaaga/suspects.json; a rule with an id used here replaces it.

rules.title: DerivedData
rules.reason: Xcode rebuilds this the next time you build. Clearing it is also the classic fix for strange build errors.

rules.title: CoreSimulator
rules.reason: Simulator devices and the apps installed on them. Devices for runtimes you no longer have are dead weight, but deleting a device loses its state.

rules.title: iOS DeviceSupport
rules.reason: Symbols for iOS versions your devices no longer run. Xcode fetches them again when you plug a device in.

rules.title: Caches
rules.reason: Temporary copies apps keep so they load faster. Apps rebuild what they need, so clearing this is safe.

rules.title: Docker.raw
rules.reason: One disk image holding every Docker image and volume. Shrink it with docker system prune or from Docker Desktop settings, not the Finder.

rules.title: iPhone Backups
rules.reason: Local iPhone and iPad backups made by the Finder. Keep your newest one; older ones are usually safe to remove.

rules.title: node_modules
rules.reason: Found in {count} project{s}. npm install brings any of them back in seconds, and nothing you wrote lives in here.

rules.title: Installers
rules.reason: Installers for apps that are already installed — {count} of them. An app does not need its installer once it has run.

rules.title: Xcode Archives
rules.reason: Builds you shipped. Keep the ones you might still need to read crash reports from.

rules.title: Homebrew downloads
rules.reason: Old package downloads. brew cleanup clears them too.

rules.title: .gradle
rules.reason: Downloaded Gradle versions and dependencies. The next build fetches what it needs.

rules.title: Trash
rules.reason: Items you already chose to delete. Emptying the Trash is what finally frees the space.
